name: Quality Management Plan
one_liner: How quality is planned, assured, controlled and improved — and where configuration management is written down.
purpose: The Quality Management Plan defines and documents the project's quality requirements, the quality management approach, process and responsibilities, and outlines the quality assurance and control activities undertaken throughout the project. It requires the balance between planned quality, cost, time and risk to be evaluated deliberately, and appropriate metrics to be defined for evaluating project management quality. The project's configuration management procedure is also documented here, so that correct versions are delivered, unauthorised changes are prevented and artefacts stay traceable.
feeds: Project Work Plan (QA/QC activities scheduled in it)

fields.what: Verify performance and compliance of project activities against defined requirements: control design, implementation and operational effectiveness, plus regulatory compliance. Usually not done by the PM.

traps: QA proves the process is being followed; QC checks results and raises change requests.
Quality Management Plan is approved by the PSC (A) — most other management plans are the PO's.
Manage Quality has SP=A, PM=R; Quality Assurance (p.58) has PM=A, PCT=R.
Configuration management lives inside the Quality Management Plan — it is not a separate PM² plan.
PM² gives no configuration registry template; you build it yourself.
